section_summary: This section closes an earlier analysis of Japan’s cotton trade, then contains a September 1939 consular report from Osaka with fourteen statistical tables. The report reviews cotton imports, industrial controls, production, exports and prices, and assesses how the war in Europe might affect Japan’s cotton supply and textile sales.

subfiles.title: Closing page of analysis of Japan’s cotton trade
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Japan’s cotton trade balance and the outlook for American cotton sales.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that American cotton sales look favorable, subject to shipping and Japanese foreign exchange permits.

subfiles.title: Japan Cotton Situation—Review and Outlook
subfiles.doc_type: consular report with index and statistical tables
subfiles.from: Walter R. McConaughy, American Consul, Osaka
subfiles.about: Reviews Japan’s 1938–39 cotton year and forecasts raw cotton demand, textile exports and staple fiber production.
subfiles.summary: The report records higher raw cotton arrivals, lower mill consumption, a sharp decline in sales to the yen currency area, and greater piece goods export volume achieved at weaker prices. It explains Japan’s production and distribution controls, mill conditions, cotton prices and foreign exchange constraints. With war beginning in Europe, it anticipates stronger demand for American cotton and Japanese textiles if credit, shipping, power, labor and import permits are available. Fourteen accompanying tables document exports, imports, consumption, production, prices, stocks and trade balances.
